correctness.rationale: The canonical genus-two double cover h:C→P1 has K_C=h^*O(1); every bicanonical zero divisor is a sum F_s+F_t of two degree-two canonical fibres with multiplicity. Every effective degree-three sub-divisor includes a full F_s or F_t, even at branch or coincident fibres, and is P+F_t; converse is immediate using F_h(P)+F_t. For any degree-three line bundle L, RR gives h0(L)=2, h1(L)=0, so Abel-Jacobi α3:Sym3 C→Pic3 C is a P1-bundle. The Abel translate T={K_C(P)} is C and its inverse image consists exactly of complete linear systems P+|K_C|; multiplication by the tautological O_C(P) section trivializes the family projectively, giving CxP1 smooth Cartier divisor. Pic3(C) is an abelian surface; adjunction gives normal T/Pic3 is K_T, pulling back gives pr_C^*K_C. Independently checked degrees and RR plus boundary fibre arguments, not relying on a saved code log.

value.rationale: The low-genus quadratic-differential incidence condition has a natural role in wobbly-bundle geometry; specifying the entire smooth subvariety and its normal class is more informative than membership counts, and directly usable in intersection/deformation calculations. It is a short special-geometry structural lemma, not a claim of a new wobbly-divisor classification or unrelated arbitrary isolated computation.

final_claim: For any smooth projective genus-two curve C over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, the degree-three divisor locus Q3(C) of sub-divisors of bicanonical zeros is the smooth divisor {P+F_t:P in C, t in P1} in Sym^3(C). It is isomorphic to C x P1, and its normal bundle is pr_C^* K_C, having degrees 2 on C-fibres and 0 on P1-fibres.
limitations: Requires smooth genus2 C in characteristic zero and degree-three effective sub-divisors of bicanonical zeros.
No claim about general g, singular curves, or deformation theory of moduli wobbly divisor; no formal proof assistant.
